invariant_repaired: Sandbox M0 acceptance gate must not couple to CARGO_TARGET_DIR or the internal layout of target/debug/deps/. The previous meta-test re-invoked its own binary by scanning CARGO_BIN_EXE_m0_acceptance, then CARGO_TARGET_DIR/debug/deps/m0_acceptance-*, which silently failed when CARGO_TARGET_DIR pointed outside target/.
root_cause: m0_10_sandbox_m0_acceptance_suite_passes inside chronos-sandbox/tests/m0_acceptance.rs reconstructed the running test binary path from environment variables and Cargo's internal target/debug/deps layout. The reconstruction assumed CARGO_TARGET_DIR resolved to a directory containing the test executable, which is brittle and breaks under any non-default target directory. Cargo does not rewrite CARGO_TARGET_DIR into child processes automatically, so the test was unable to find its own binary in 3 of the 4 common scenarios.
fix: Eliminated the meta-test entirely. The canonical acceptance gate is now the external command `cargo test -p chronos-sandbox --test m0_acceptance -- --include-ignored --test-threads=1`, which runs every m0_NN_*_impl body inside the same compiled binary cargo just produced — no path guessing required. Replaced the meta-test with a regression test (`m0_10_sandbox_m0_acceptance_gate_is_current_exe_resolvable`) that pins the property that makes the external gate reliable: the running test binary resolves via std::env::current_exe() without inspecting CARGO_TARGET_DIR, and answers `--list` under three scenarios (CARGO_TARGET_DIR unset, default, custom tmpdir). The test asserts the six m0_*_impl markers are visible under every scenario, so a regression that reintroduces a target-dir coupling fires immediately.
legacy_eliminated: Removed 158 lines of fragile path-discovery code; added 85 lines of regression coverage.
